To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synthesis of the mature F-pili subunit requires the activity of traQ and traG gene products.

The synthesis of mature F-pilin requires the expression of 2 tra operons in addition to the traA gene, that the traQ gene product processes the traA product to yield a polypeptide of apparent molecular weight 7,000 which is the major product of traA in the presence of tra Q, and that a polypeptide with an apparent molecular mass of approximately 7,000 is the mature F pilin subunit.
synthesis of a mature subunit of the F-pilus requires expression of at least two tra genes in addition to traA and that traA expression results in the synthesis of an Ap14 precursor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of tra genes and their products involved in synthesis and assembly of F-pilin and F-pili, and we propose a model for the synthesis of these structures.
the identification of the gene products involved, and the pathway for the assembly, of the F-pili.

the identification of the gene products which participate in the synthesis of the F pilus, and the identification of the steps involved in the synthesis and assembly of F-pilin, the subunit of the F-pilus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
traQ and traG activities appear to be required for synthesis of a mature subunit of the pilus, and that traQ activity may be required for the initial processing of the polypeptide product of traA.
traQ is required for the processing of Ap7(Q) to Ap7* and traG is required for the assembly of the mature F-pilus subunits into the pilus structure.
synthesis of the F- pili requires at least 4 tra operon genes, traA, traG, traQ, and traT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the traA gene product is synthesized as a 14,000 molecular weight polypeptide, which may be modified to a 7,000 molecular weight product by a traQ product.
the F-pilin structural gene, traA, encodes a 14,000 dalton precursor, which requires the traQ product for processing.

the synthesis of F pilus requires the expression of 5 tra operon genes: traA, traG, traQ, traJ, and traD, and that the expression of the traJ and traD genes are not required for assembly of a pilus structure, but are required for efficient assembly of F-pilus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the F-pilin structural gene product is processed to a mature subunit which is assembled into pili.
traQ is required to process the Ap14 product of the tra A gene to yield the Ap7(Q) precursor of the mature F-piliin subunit.
synthesis of the F pilus is a complicated process that requires the expression of several tra genes in addition to traA.
